statement: Today Marta is 40 years old and her son is 12. In how many years' time will Marta be exactly twice as old as her son?

choices.misconception: I worked out how old the son will be at that moment and gave his age instead of the number of years.
I added the years to the son's age but not to Marta's, so I solved 40 = 2 x (12 + x).
I worked out how old Marta will be at that moment instead of how many years away it is.
I halved the 28-year age gap, thinking the son only has to make up half of it.

hints: Does the difference between their ages ever change?
Age problems have one fixed quantity: the age gap. When Marta is twice as old as her son, the gap between them equals the son's age at that moment.
The gap is 40 - 12 = 28 years, so at that moment the son will be 28. How many years from now is that?

solutions.reliable: In x years Marta will be 40 + x and her son 12 + x. Twice as old means 40 + x = 2(12 + x) = 24 + 2x, so x = 16. Check: in 16 years they will be 56 and 28, and 56 is twice 28. The transferable idea: in age problems every person gets older by the same number of years.
solutions.elegant: The age gap is always 28 years. When Marta is twice her son's age, the gap equals the son's age, so he will be 28. He is 12 now, so that is 16 years away.

whyOnTest: Age problems reward spotting that the age gap never changes, and each trap answer either ages only one person or answers a different question.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
